already-have.reason:
Not implemented and not refuted, but most of the six checklist rows are already normative in the frozen Draft 1.1 or are Trezor copy-model artefacts that do not transfer to an A/B select design. The repo_evidence facts are true today: the legacy try-once arbitration is still live (fsbl/src/main.rs:384-411), the only boot_state writer is CMD_FW_COMMIT (secure/src/nsc/cmd_fw_commit.rs:250; secure/src/hw/boot_state.rs:129-141), the Route-1 journal pages 64/122 are reserved with no consumer outside geometry tests (geometry/src/lib.rs:122-128), and the v6 journal QW layout is constants only (fw-manifest/src/v6.rs:79-100).

Row by row against Draft 1.1 (docs/security/a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md):
- (a) Hash binding: already specified. The arm-token preimage binds install_id, signed_manifest_digest, secure_hash and nonsecure_hash (:2066-2073), and only the immutable decoder may construct the key (:2115-2117).
- (b) Idempotent apply and erase-record-first: this is Trezor's copy model. Draft 1.1 uses write-once QWs that are never retried (:3788-3789), which is a different and stricter discipline, so the row would contradict the frozen design rather than add to it.
- (c) FSBL re-verify: inherent, since the FSBL verifies on every boot and accepts only schema 0x06 / PQFW_V6 (:1976-1978).
- (d) Range and magic validation: frozen offsets with compile-time pins (fw-manifest/src/v6.rs:107 onward). I did not audit the non-overlap and both-sides double-check wording line by line.
- (e) Reserved schema/flags byte for route-around: the genuine delta, and it collides with the freeze. Draft 1.1 deliberately has schema exact 0x06, header reserved exact zero and trailing reserved exact 0xFF (:1828-1846), a "true flag day" (:1976), and FROZEN-MAN-4 requires a new reviewed digest for any byte change (:666-674). A frozen FSBL also cannot honour a flag it has a bug handling. Trezor's own workaround (BOARDLOADER_UCB_ZERO_ADDR_BUG) lives in the mutable producer and needs no record field.
- (f) Confirm written by the runtime after a health milestone, never by the FSBL: already normative (:233-235, :5244-5270; memory project_ab_rollback_spec_review.md).

The torn-state rule is likewise already fail-closed in the spec (:3786-3789, with Recovering/Unknown forbidding handoff at :399 and :2304) and tracked as #138. What survives is a small review-process item: a traceability table mapping the Trezor UCB invariants to Draft 1.1 sections for the FA-1.3 / #546 Phase-D reviewers, plus a mutable-producer route-around principle and a canonical journal-encoding corpus.
already-have.corrections:
1. Reframe from "amend the Draft 1.1 spec" to "add a non-normative traceability checklist to the FA-1.3 (#540) and FA-PG1b (#546) review prompts". Amending the text is a re-freeze event (new digest, both reviewers, owner; docs/security/fw-rollback-freeze-receipt-2026-07-26.md:82-83, 147; #545 authority envelope). The proposal's own risk line admits this, which makes it cost M, not S, if done as an amendment.
2. Drop row (b). It is Trezor copy semantics; Draft 1.1 never erases or retries journal QWs (:3788-3789).
3. Rewrite row (e). Do not add a flags byte to the FSBL-consumed record, which conflicts with FROZEN-MAN-4, the exact-zero/0xFF reserved bytes and the flag-day rule (:666-674, :1828-1846, :1976). Replace it with: (i) a stated principle that every FSBL-consumed encoding is produced only by mutable code, so a frozen-decoder bug is routed around by constraining the producer, as Trezor's flag actually does; (ii) a pre-freeze differential or fuzz corpus of the FSBL journal/manifest decoder against the host pure core, so the frozen decoder's accepted set is known before WRP + RDP-2.
4. Rows (a), (c) and (f) are already normative. List them as "verify the implementation matches", not as new spec rows.
5. The repo_evidence line "no schema/flags QW for route-around" is true for the five journal QWs but omits that the manifest page already carries a schema byte at offset 4 and reserved fields (fw-manifest/src/v6.rs:67-69), deliberately pinned to exact values.
6. The legacy arbitration evidence is accurate but already slated for deletion: #758 records the owner decision to drop the try-once guard, parked on the secure-side pointer_gate FI gate. The legacy defects are tracked by #271 and #138 and are not new.
7. The "fsbl-tests source_invariants pins" follow-up is reasonable but belongs to #546 acceptance; nothing can be pinned until the journal consumer exists.

feasible.reason:
The threat is real for the legacy bench code (#138 and #271 are open, and fsbl/src/main.rs:386-399 still has the "TRIED + unreadable boot-state means try the winner" arm), but the proposal's premises about the replacement design are false, and one of its six rows is unsound.

1. Wrong object. The "Route-1 journal" (pages 64/122) is not the A/B activation control record. FROZEN-ROUTE1-1 (docs/security/a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:1256-1366) defines it as the OTP-floor launch pre-claim journal. It is written only by the FSBL itself (FsblRollbackWriter, :2252-2254) and is never touched on any T==F field path (:1362-1364). The record that plays the Trezor UCB role is the manifest-page lifecycle (QW_PENDING, two CONFIRMED replicas, the TAMP ARM_READY/ATTEMPTED token; fw-manifest/src/v6.rs:80-89, spec §6.2). The proposal cites the v6.rs journal quad-words as if they were the Route-1 layout.

2. "No schema/flags" is false. The manifest has OFF_SCHEMA=4 / SCHEMA_V6, and the decoder hard-rejects any other value (v6.rs:561-563). It also rejects non-zero header-reserved bytes (:565) and non-erased trailing-reserved bytes (:592). Route-1 carries versioned domain bytes (PQJ1SNP etc., spec :1282-1285) and requires reserved QWs 80-505 to stay erased (:1277).

3. Rows (a), (c), (d), (f) and the torn-state rule are already normative in Draft 1.1.
- (a)/(c): §7.1 VerifiedArtifact has the FSBL re-check structure/CRC, slot binding, signed digest, C10 signature, floor, and both image lengths and hashes (:2585-2598).
- (d): no record carries an address at all. "No raw address, manifest field ... can select a destination", with maps checked twice (:2283-2288). This is stricter than Trezor's check-then-dereference.
- (f): CandidateFinalizationWriter runs in the booted candidate and consumes a RuntimeFinalizationReceipt after the §8/§9 health milestones (:2249-2251, :3120-3192). The FSBL only writes ARM_READY to ATTEMPTED.
- Torn state: torn or ambiguous terminal evidence never falls through to PENDING (:590-603), and Unknown halts (:2556-2558).
- Acceptance rows already exist in §15 (:4671-4678, :4956) and §16 (:5247).

4. Row (b) does not transfer. Trezor erases the UCB to stop the boardloader re-copying on every boot. pq1 selects rather than copies, and its lifecycle is program-only quad-words. An "erase the record first" step is a new mutation that no writer in §6.3 owns and it contradicts the frozen writer map.

5. Row (e) is unsound. A frozen FSBL can only honour a flag it was coded to honour before the freeze, so a reserved byte cannot route around a bug nobody knew about. A flag the FSBL does honour is a new input to the immutable decoder, controlled by the mutable (possibly hostile) runtime, that disables or reinterprets a check. That is a downgrade knob, and it contradicts the strict reserved-must-be-erased rules and the 2026-07-26 errata. The Trezor precedent shows the opposite mechanism: the workaround is the mutable producer avoiding the bug-triggering input (never staging code_address==0), with no field in the UCB (boot_ucb.h:30-42 has only magic, two addresses, padding, hash).

Net: nothing needs building and no board change is needed, but the deliverable as written is roughly 80% duplication, one inapplicable row and one harmful row. Any amendment reopens the Draft 1.1 digest (dual review plus owner re-ratification), so cost S is not honest.
feasible.corrections:
Salvageable residue: do not amend Draft 1.1. Record a short cross-check note (in the #546 / FA-2 review inputs or the existing adversarial-review playbook) with three points.
- A Trezor-UCB-to-Draft-1.1 mapping table showing (a), (c), (d), (f) are already covered, with the section cites above.
- An explicit statement that route-around of a frozen-FSBL bug is producer-side input avoidance only. The mutable runtime must be able to choose encodings inside the already-accepted set; no FSBL-honoured disable/reinterpret flag is permitted.
- Before the freeze, require that FSBL record decoders are total and strict and are differentially fuzzed against the host model. This is already the direction of §15.1.

Factual errors to fix in the proposal:
- "Route-1 journal" should be the manifest-page lifecycle journal (QW_PENDING / CONFIRMED_0/1 plus TAMP token). Route-1 (pages 64/122) is the OTP-launch pre-claim journal, written by the FSBL itself.
- "No schema/flags QW" is wrong: the schema byte is at offset 4 and is strictly checked (v6.rs:561-563).
- Row (a) misstates the precedent. The Trezor UCB hash covers only the boot header (boot_ucb.c:108-119, :131-137). The code is bound via the signed Merkle root in the boardloader (boardloader/main.c:187-194), not by a SHA-256 of the staged artifact.
- Row (f) is not "copied from boot_ucb.c / boardloader main.c". Trezor has no TRIED-to-COMMITTED confirm-alive concept in those files.
- The cited Trezor line ranges are accurate (boot_ucb.c:56-171, boardloader main.c:148-250, bootloader main.c:496-500, model_T3W1.h:56-68). However, at checkout 6ab39e95cf BOARDLOADER_UCB_ZERO_ADDR_BUG has no consumer anywhere in the tree; a repo-wide grep finds only the #define. The claim "the fix lives in the mutable bootloader as a workaround flag" is supported only by the comment, not by code. Current boot_ucb.c:38-46 does exempt the 0 sentinel.
- The legacy defects cited (fsbl/src/main.rs:384-411, boot_state.rs) are real, but they are bench-only, production-fenced, and already tracked in #138 and #271. They are not evidence that Draft 1.1 re-creates them.
- The proposal targets "Draft 1.1", but a Draft 1.2 delta candidate exists (docs/security/fw-rollback-draft12-candidate-2026-07-21.md) that inherits §6-§7 unchanged. Any note should be attached there or to #546, not to a new amendment.

Kind stays process; no hardware change. Cost is S only if delivered as a non-normative cross-check note, and M or more if it amends the spec. Priority P3.
